items.claim: The frame-opening span is argued without touching the bytes that close the preceding frame, and its name-spelling digit reasons from four verses outside the span that carry no matching evidence ref.
items.evidence: The onset at 52:1 stands immediately after oshb:Jer.51.64, whose bytes close with the colophon עַד הֵ֖נָּה דִּבְרֵ֥י יִרְמְיָֽהוּ (oshb:Jer.51.64, byte) - the book's own closing statement, standing on the verse immediately before this onset - and that same verse carries a SAMEKH (single-witness WLC; tier-3 weak in the Prophets; absence never counterevidence). Neither is engaged anywhere in the span's prose, so the declared false-positive disposition on this seam-verse mark gap is refuted: it is a live disclosure gap on the exact verse whose bytes bear on this onset, not a heuristic artifact. Inside the span the handling is sound - the ketiv/qere over the queen mother's name at oshb:Jer.52.1 and the paseq at oshb:Jer.52.3 (single-witness WLC, count-only, no position asserted) are both disclosed, the chapter's next paseq site is 52:15 and its single parashah mark stands at 52:30 (1 marked verse in this chapter), and the three quoted runs at oshb:Jer.52.1, oshb:Jer.52.2 and oshb:Jer.52.3 re-collate at byte tier. Reading 52:1 as an age-at-accession formula rather than a dated frame is byte-correct and is not contested. The Zedekiah digit is also correct - the long spelling צִדְקִיָּ֣הוּ (oshb:Jer.52.1, byte) stands in six verses of this chapter, 52:1, 52:3, 52:5, 52:8, 52:10, 52:11 (sweep: 6 verses; 44 verses book-wide) - but 52:5, 52:8, 52:10 and 52:11 are argued in prose from outside the span while the evidence refs stop at 52:3.
tier_citations: parashah SAMEKH, single-witness WLC, tier-3 weak

items.claim: The stated ground for holding 52:4-52:11 whole - that no fresh date breaks the chain - is contested by 52:6, which opens its verse with a month-and-day dating notice in the same shape treated as boundary-bearing at 52:12.
items.evidence: 52:6 opens asyndetically with בַּחֹ֤דֶשׁ הָֽרְבִיעִי֙ בְּתִשְׁעָ֣ה לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ (oshb:Jer.52.6, byte): month ordinal plus day, verse-initial, and undisclosed anywhere in the span. The chapter's next dating notice carries the identical shape with only a prefixed vav and a mid-verse year gloss, וּבַחֹ֤דֶשׁ הַֽחֲמִישִׁי֙ בֶּעָשׂ֣וֹר לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ (oshb:Jer.52.12, byte), and that shape is treated as a fresh onset at 52:12. The span does clear the weaker shape at 52:5 explicitly and correctly - עַ֚ד עַשְׁתֵּ֣י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.52.5, byte) is a terminus rather than an onset - which makes the silence over the stronger verse-initial shape at 52:6 an asymmetry within the same class rather than a uniform decision about it; the English paragraph break at that verse is tier-4 and carries no weight in either direction. Whether 52:6 should cut is arguable, since its date sits inside the siege the 52:4 frame already opens; what the bytes will not carry is the categorical wording that no fresh date breaks the chain. Everything else verifies: the verse-initial frame at 52:4 is byte-true, the runs quoted at oshb:Jer.52.4, oshb:Jer.52.5, oshb:Jer.52.9 and oshb:Jer.52.11 all re-collate at byte tier, the ketiv/qere at oshb:Jer.52.11 is disclosed and no paseq or parashah mark falls in 52:4-52:11, and the name digit is right - the resh-family spelling stands in five verses of this chapter, 52:4, 52:12, 52:28, 52:29, 52:30 (sweep: 5 verses; 29 verses book-wide for that spelling).

items.claim: The span's cohesion argument folds 52:14 under the newly named captain of the guard, but that verse's bytes predicate its action of the Chaldean army, and the span's own paseq goes undisclosed while the same layer is disclosed at the chapter's other paseq sites.
items.evidence: The span is carried by the clause 'What he does under that dating stays one span', yet 52:14 reads וְאֶת כָּל חֹמ֥וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם סָבִ֑יב נָֽתְצוּ֙ כָּל חֵ֣יל כַּשְׂדִּ֔ים (oshb:Jer.52.14, byte) - the wall-breaking is predicated of the Chaldean army, with the captain of the guard entering only as the party they are with - so the middle of the span has two acting subjects, not one. No Hebrew is quoted from 52:13-52:15 at all, so that stretch is asserted rather than engaged. A paseq stands at oshb:Jer.52.15 inside the span (single-witness WLC, count-only) and is not disclosed, while the layer is disclosed at this chapter's other paseq sites 52:3 and 52:25; there is no ketiv/qere and no parashah mark in 52:12-52:16. The onset itself holds and both quoted runs re-collate at byte tier: the month-first notice at 52:12 is byte-true and the agent it introduces is real, נְבֽוּזַרְאֲדָן֙ רַב טַבָּחִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.52.12, byte) standing in five verses of this chapter, 52:12, 52:15, 52:16, 52:26, 52:30 (sweep: 5 verses; 11 verses book-wide), with the bare title standing without the name at 52:14, 52:19 and 52:24 (sweep: 8 verses in this chapter carry the title) - both digits exactly as stated. One wording caveat: the contrast drawn against a verse-initial shape is between year-first and month-first shapes, since 52:12's notice is itself verse-initial.

items.claim: The 52:17 seam rests on a change of catalogued object, while the construction and the subject change it relies on both already stand inside the preceding stretch; and the span's paseq is undisclosed although a ketiv/qere in the same span is engaged.
items.evidence: 52:17 opens וְאֶת עַמּוּדֵ֨י הַנְּחֹ֜שֶׁת and predicates שִׁבְּר֣וּ כַשְׂדִּ֑ים (oshb:Jer.52.17, byte). The same fronted vav-plus-object construction with the same subject already stands at 52:14, וְאֶת כָּל חֹמ֥וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם סָבִ֑יב נָֽתְצוּ֙ כָּל חֵ֣יל כַּשְׂדִּ֔ים (oshb:Jer.52.14, byte), and the acting subject alternates across 52:14 (Chaldean army), 52:15-52:16 (the captain of the guard) and 52:17 (Chaldeans) - so neither the construction nor a subject change distinguishes 52:17 from points inside the preceding stretch where no cut is made. No dating notice and no speech formula stands at 52:17, leaving a change of inventoried object as the whole warrant, and confidence is nonetheless declared high. A paseq stands at oshb:Jer.52.20 (single-witness WLC, count-only) - inside the verse quoted at length - and is not disclosed, while the ketiv/qere at oshb:Jer.52.21 is: one engaged mark in the span owes the other. The verified parts: both quoted runs re-collate at byte tier; the ketiv/qere description at oshb:Jer.52.21 matches the bytes; and the numeral read at 52:20 is right - שְׁנֵים עָשָׂ֤ר (oshb:Jer.52.20, byte) is the cardinal-teen, and the same consonantal string carries the year sense elsewhere in the book, שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֡ים (oshb:Jer.34.14, byte); that string is a contiguous consonantal substring that also lands inside unrelated tokens (substring sweep: 9 verses book-wide), so the confirmation is per-site rather than by digit.

items.claim: The closure argument reads the Judah token at 52:27 as the same named land the chapter's opening makes the scene, but the bytes give the token two different roles and name a different word for the land, and the opening verse is argued from outside the span with no matching evidence ref.
items.evidence: 52:27 closes וַיִּ֥גֶל יְהוּדָ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל אַדְמָתֽוֹ (oshb:Jer.52.27, byte): Judah is the exiled subject and the land is the suffixed noun, not the toponym. At 52:3 the same token stands inside the locative pair בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֣ם וִֽיהוּדָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.52.3, byte) belonging to the divine-anger clause, while the rebellion clause of that verse names only the king and the king of Babylon - so naming the same land as the scene of both the rebellion and the exile is not what the two verses say. A byte-true hook between them does exist and is unused: the repeated preposition-plus-suffix, מֵעַ֣ל פָּנָ֑יו (oshb:Jer.52.3, byte) against מֵעַ֥ל אַדְמָתֽוֹ (oshb:Jer.52.27, byte). 52:3 is argued in prose from outside the span while the evidence refs reach only to 52:23 on that side. The rest holds: both quoted runs re-collate at byte tier, the office-versus-role contrast at 52:24 and 52:25 is byte-true, and the disclosure is complete for the span - the paseq at oshb:Jer.52.25 is disclosed (single-witness WLC, count-only) and no ketiv/qere or parashah mark falls in 52:24-52:27.

items.claim: The three-entry census holds as one span on its own bytes: the date-shape split, the name digit, the parashah type and the span's full mark disclosure all verify.
items.evidence: 52:28 opens the governing nominal clause זֶ֣ה הָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶגְלָ֖ה נְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֑ר with its year word standing after that clause (oshb:Jer.52.28, byte), while 52:29 and 52:30 both open on the year word itself - a header-internal shape against two verse-initial ones, exactly the split argued. 52:29 carries no finite verb of its own and hangs on the 52:28 predicate, and the set is closed by the summing clause כָּל נֶ֕פֶשׁ אַרְבַּ֥עַת אֲלָפִ֖ים וְשֵׁ֥שׁ מֵאֽוֹת (oshb:Jer.52.30, byte), which is the strongest byte ground for holding the three entries together. The parashah mark at oshb:Jer.52.30 is correctly typed as a petuchah and is the only parashah mark in this chapter (1 marked verse in this chapter; 303 marked verses book-wide; single-witness WLC; tier-3 weak; absence never counterevidence), and no paseq and no ketiv/qere falls in 52:28-52:30, so the span's disclosure is complete. Both quoted runs re-collate at byte tier and the name digit is right: the resh-family spelling stands in all three verses (sweep: 3 verses). One qualification the bytes add rather than break - 52:30 carries its own predicate with a different subject, הֶגְלָ֗ה נְבֽוּזַרְאֲדָן֙ רַב טַבָּחִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.52.30, byte), so the third entry is bound to the header at the level of the census rather than by a shared clause; the declared close-call reading and the medium confidence already carry that weight.
tier_citations: parashah PE, single-witness WLC, tier-3 weak

items.claim: The onset frame is misdescribed: the verse-initial date reckons by the Judean king's exile, not by a Babylonian king's accession, and the accession reading rests on an ordinal the Hebrew does not carry.
items.evidence: 52:31 opens וַיְהִי֩ בִשְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וָשֶׁ֜בַע שָׁנָ֗ה לְגָלוּת֙ יְהוֹיָכִ֣ן מֶֽלֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.52.31, byte) - thirty-seven years reckoned to the exile of the king of Judah. The Babylonian reckoning is a separate, mid-verse element, בִּשְׁנַ֣ת מַלְכֻת֗וֹ (oshb:Jer.52.31, byte), which carries no ordinal at all, so “in the first year of his reign” (web:Jer.52.31) is the English rendering's supplement; the description of the opening frame as dated to a Babylonian king's own accession therefore states of the verse-initial frame what the bytes place mid-verse and what the Hebrew does not say, and the same wording is reused as the ground for not folding the notice back into the preceding census. The verse also carries two date elements, not one, so a single verse-initial signal does not describe its shape completely. The boundary itself is not contested and the rest is strong: both quoted runs re-collate at byte tier; the two Jehoiachin spellings inside 52:31 are real and each stands exactly once in the book, defective יְהוֹיָכִ֣ן (oshb:Jer.52.31, byte) in the dating clause against plene יְהוֹיָכִ֣ין (oshb:Jer.52.31, byte) in the head-lifting clause (sweep: 1 verse each), and neither is the Jeconiah or the Coniah form; the ketiv/qere at oshb:Jer.52.31 and the ketiv/qere at oshb:Jer.52.32 are both disclosed and both match the bytes; the preceding petuchah at oshb:Jer.52.30 is correctly typed (single-witness WLC, tier-3 weak); and no paseq falls in 52:31-52:34.
tier_citations: parashah PE, single-witness WLC, tier-3 weak
